findings.evidence: NEVER align columns with tabs: viewers use different tab stops, so columns drift. Use spaces.
findings.fix: Keep the useful formatting constraints concise and add design-specific decision guidance grounded in observed wireframe failures; record any removal of instructions the model reliably produces unprompted.

findings.evidence: ## Gotchas
findings.fix: Supplement the formatting warnings with a concrete UI-mockup failure and its consequence, such as showing an error solely through color when the ASCII handoff must communicate it in text.

findings.evidence: questions in steps 1 and 5 end the run ... If the user rejects all, ask which ranked task each option got wrong, then redraw.
findings.fix: State that the agent returns the rejection question to the caller and redraws on a subsequent invocation with the user's answer, or redraws immediately only when that feedback is already available.

findings.evidence: Default to 3 structurally distinct mockups (not restyles of one layout) ... draw the third by varying the other axis (density or navigation) on the best-fit structure.
findings.fix: Clarify that the third alternative may deliberately reuse a structure when the task branch yields fewer than three viable structures, and identify the substantive trade-off it must demonstrate.

findings.evidence: Show scroll regions with `^`/`v` edge marks and modals as an inner box over the base screen.
findings.fix: Move the scroll and modal drawing convention into a skill this plugin bundles (for example references/ascii-conventions.md, preloaded via skills:) so the body keeps only the width, ranking and handoff rules the agent would not derive.

findings.evidence: NEVER write implementation code: no layout is picked yet, so code locks in one alternative and is wasted.
findings.fix: Add the exception the workflow already allows: NEVER write implementation code before a pick, because it locks one unchosen alternative; after step 6, write code only if the caller asks, and keep the component map as the default handoff.

findings.evidence: Classify the dominant task and vary one structural axis per alternative: compare records -> aligned table vs cards; inspect one item -> master/detail if both panes fit the width, else a single detail view; complete a sequence -> wizard if later steps depend on earlier answers, else one form.
findings.fix: Keep the table/cards, master-detail and wizard defaults, and add one escape: when the user names a structure outside those three (kanban, split composer, command palette), draw that structure as one of the three alternatives and say which axis it replaces.

findings.evidence: If the task branch yields only one or two structures, draw the third by varying the other axis (density or navigation) on the best-fit structure, and say so.
findings.fix: Name the order: vary navigation first (top, side, none), then density (compact vs spacious) on the best-fit structure, and if both axes are already used, repeat the best-fit structure with the overflow rule applied differently and say which axis was exhausted.

findings.evidence: `base=origin`, except fork PRs: if an `upstream` remote exists ... and the PR base lives there ... set `base=upstream`
findings.fix: For a fork PR, identify the base repository and a matching local remote before selecting the base. If no matching remote exists or its identity cannot be established, stop and ask the user to configure or identify it; do not silently use the fork's origin.

findings.evidence: `gh pr view --json url,isCrossRepository` when available
findings.fix: Before relying on the version-sensitive `gh pr view` JSON fields, inspect the installed CLI's supported fields, or cite the official `gh pr view` documentation and the date checked alongside the instruction; retain the ask-user fallback if the fields are unavailable.

findings.evidence: Never use `--force` or `-f`, even after a lease rejection. A background `git fetch` (IDE, cron) moves the remote-tracking ref and silently disarms a bare `--force-with-lease`
findings.fix: Keep the background-fetch lease gotcha. Drop the standalone 'never --force' clause (the model already refuses a bare force-push) and record that removal in docs/audit/recovery/sync-branch/record.md.

findings.evidence: Run each step in order; stop at the first failed check and report it.
findings.fix: Before step 1, add the decision the order is protecting: which ref is the true base (fork upstream vs origin), whether the published tip is yours alone, and whether the replay root is fork-point, the pre-fetch old base, or a plain rebase. Then run the numbered steps.

findings.evidence: Never `git pull` (it merges or rebases the feature branch's own remote, the wrong upstream), never `git merge` (the merge commit breaks the PR's linear history).
findings.fix: Add the missing landmine: NEVER `git rebase --skip` a conflicted commit, because the feature change is dropped and the next push looks clean. Leave the rebase paused and let the user resolve, continue, or abort.

findings.evidence: Not for merge-based sync, updating local main, or rebasing a branch others push to.
findings.fix: Rebase the current feature branch onto the latest origin/main (or a given target) and update its PR with --force-with-lease. Use when a feature branch or PR is behind, out of date or conflicts with its base, or the user asks to update, catch up or sync a branch, even without the word rebase. Not for merge-based sync, updating local main, creating a branch, or rebasing a branch others push to.

findings.evidence: (b) If `fork` is non-empty and differs from `plain`, `fork` is always the newer commit, so list what fork-point would skip
findings.fix: Keep the ask, but state the default when the user is not there to answer: stop and change nothing. Skip only on an explicit 'skip'; a plain rebase only on an explicit 'keep'.

findings.evidence: if an `upstream` remote exists (`git remote`) and the PR base lives there (`gh pr view --json url,isCrossRepository` when available, taking owner/repo from the PR `url` as the base repository, else ask once), set `base=upstream`
findings.fix: Resolve the unmatched case: if `gh` is missing, returns no PR, or errors, or the url's owner/repo matches neither `upstream` nor `origin`, ask once which remote is the base and stop on anything but a named remote. Never guess `upstream` from the remote existing alone.

findings.evidence: `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` not empty (a modified or staged tracked file): stop
findings.fix: Also stop when `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` is non-empty or any of `MERGE_HEAD`, `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`, `REBASE_HEAD` or `BISECT_LOG` exists, before recording state. Step 1 currently lets unmerged index entries and a bisect through to the rebase.

findings.evidence: The dbff837f digest says "removed units (95, showing 40)"; the remaining 55 removal items are not individually available in the prompt.
findings.fix: Provide the complete digest so every removed unit can be checked against the current files and docs/audit/recovery/writing-clearly-and-concisely/record.md.

findings.evidence: "Protected quoted material ... is never rewritten in any branch."
findings.fix: Allow an explicit request to edit the user's own quoted dialogue or draft to override the default. For attributed testimony or legal quotations, distinguish proposed edits from the original and do not misrepresent an altered quotation as verbatim.

findings.evidence: Load at most the one section that answers the open question; the rules above cover ordinary tightening without any reference. When context is tight, read only that section and edit locally.
findings.fix: The model already knows to load less when context is tight. Delete that second sentence and record the removal in docs/audit/recovery/writing-clearly-and-concisely/record.md; keep the load table, which gates the files.

findings.evidence: NEVER lists three failures the checkpoints do not catch, but there is no Gotchas section for environment-specific facts that defy assumptions.
findings.fix: Add a short Gotchas section after NEVER naming only failures this skill actually meets: a rewrite that is no shorter still counts as done when an invariant required it; a heading's text is its anchor, so renaming it breaks inbound links; a cleaned-up error string no longer matches the log. Do not pad it with items the task never meets.

findings.evidence: The composition row says to read elements-of-style/03 and then 'the matching rule (8-9 paragraphs, 10 active voice, 13 needless words, 16 related words, 18 emphasis)' and to skip the other rules, but names no heading text to stop at.
findings.fix: Name the heading to read and the next heading to stop before, for example Rule 13 through the line before Rule 14, so the agent does not load the rest of the file.

findings.evidence: Notes, one short line each, only when they apply, then later 'In Edit and Structure they come after the rewrite, and only for protected quoted material or when the user asks for an explanation of the changes (then at most 5 items); the one-line note limits above apply only when no explanation was asked for.'
findings.fix: State one default: after an Edit or Structure rewrite, emit only the one-line notes that apply, and add the quoted-fragment suggestion list only for protected quoted material or when the user asked why, capped at 5. Leave the Flag branch's separate cap of about 10.

findings.evidence: Ten should-trigger and ten should-not-trigger queries, but the negatives are far misses (diagnose a slow query, translate to French, count words, summarize a log, fix a syntax error, write unit tests, check for leaked secrets, explain a re-render, extract error strings). Only 'my status report sounds like ChatGPT wrote it' is a near miss.
findings.fix: Replace several obvious negatives with near misses that share this skill's words but belong elsewhere: a request to humanize a draft without cutting meaning, a request to write a README from scratch for a product the user describes, and a request to copyedit code comments or a docstring. Keep the count near 10 and 10.

findings.evidence: Pick the branch maps a long document that repeats itself to Structure, and Structure step 1 says the default when the user did not authorise restructuring is to keep every heading and consolidate only the prose inside each section.
findings.fix: Add a row or a sentence: a long document that repeats itself but whose request does not say restructure, reorganize or merge goes to Edit, section by section, and Structure's merge is used only when the user authorises it. State that an unauthorised merge is the failure NEVER already names.

findings.evidence: Draft branch step 2 specifies an error message (quote the failing identifier, name the fix, add Needs: remediation, no apology), but steps 1 and 3 are the only instructions for a README, policy, UI string or report.
findings.fix: Add one Draft line for non-error prose: one fact per sentence, every specific through the claims checkpoint, brand voice only from a supplied sample, and end with Needs: lines for anything missing. Do not add a template menu.
